description: A high-achieving student who excels in theoretical data structures and logic but feels intimidated by the transition from high-level languages like Python to systems-level C programming.

nodes.personalizationRationale: As this student has no prior exposure to systems programming, we provide a primer on C pointers and memory which are essential for understanding OS kernels.
nodes.description: A foundational primer on C programming, focusing on pointers, memory addresses, and the stack/heap, which are prerequisites for understanding OS kernel operations.
nodes.title: C Programming for Systems Basics
Computer Architecture & OS Interface
nodes.description: An overview of computer architecture from an OS perspective, including registers, the program counter, and how the CPU interacts with main memory.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the no_prior_exposure tier, a review of hardware-software interaction is necessary before diving into OS services.

nodes.title: Systems Development Environment Setup
nodes.description: Introduction to the Unix command line, the GCC compiler toolchain, and basic Makefile usage for compiling system-level code.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student's no_prior_exposure status requires a hands-on introduction to the command line environment used for OS assignments.

nodes.title: OS Foundations & Kernel Structures
nodes.description: Exploration of OS services, system call interfaces, and the fundamental distinction between kernel mode and user mode.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node establishes the fundamental structure of an OS, required for all students regardless of their background.

nodes.title: Process Lifecycle & Operations
nodes.description: Understanding the process control block (PCB), process states, and the mechanics of process creation via fork() and exec().
nodes.personalizationRationale: Process management is a foundational concept that every student must master for the cumulative exams.
IPC is essential for understanding how complex systems are built, forming a core part of the syllabus.
nodes.description: Comparing shared memory and message passing models for communication between independent processes.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)

nodes.personalizationRationale: Threading is a mandatory topic that introduces the complexities of concurrency required for later synchronization modules.
nodes.description: Transitioning from processes to threads, covering multithreading models, concurrency benefits, and threading libraries like Pthreads.
nodes.title: Threads & Concurrency Models
CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.description: Analyzing CPU scheduling criteria and algorithms like Round Robin, Priority, and Multi-level Queue scheduling.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core topic is vital for understanding system performance and resource allocation.

nodes.description: A comprehensive review session and practice exam covering Chapters 1 through 5 in preparation for the week 8 midterm.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a required assessment node, this ensures the student is prepared for the first 20% of their final grade.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Processes & Scheduling

nodes.description: Addressing the critical section problem using hardware and software solutions like Mutexes and Semaphores.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a core course objective and is heavily tested on both projects and the final exam.
nodes.title: Process Synchronization Primitives
Classic Problems of Synchronization
nodes.description: Applying synchronization tools to classic problems like the Bounded-Buffer, Readers-Writers, and Dining Philosophers.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student must be able to model synchronization analytically to succeed in the final exam.

nodes.title: Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Deadlock management is a mandatory, though smaller, component of the OS concepts every student must master.
nodes.description: Defining deadlock conditions and exploring strategies for prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and detection.

nodes.title: Main Memory & Paging Mechanisms
nodes.description: Hardware-based memory management, including address binding, logical vs physical address spaces, and basic paging.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Memory management is a core syllabus pillar and essential for the upcoming project deliveries.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
nodes.description: Deep dive into demand paging, page replacement algorithms (LRU, FIFO, Optimal), and the problem of thrashing.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Virtual memory concepts are advanced core requirements that are central to modern OS design.

nodes.title: I/O Systems & File Storage Implementation
nodes.description: Overview of I/O hardware, kernel I/O subsystems, and the structural implementation of file systems on disk.
nodes.personalizationRationale: I/O and File Systems represent the final mandatory block of the syllabus, integrating memory and process concepts.

nodes.description: A final cumulative review session covering all textbook chapters from the foundations through I/O, preparing for the cumulative final.
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory assessment node to ensure the student can synthesize the entire course for the 40% final exam.
nodes.title: Final Cumulative Course Review
